summary: Sustained 5xx surge for streaming sessions due to connection-hold head-of-line and upstream thread-fairness starvation
description: Issue summary: Ledgerly reported a sustained increase in 5xx errors for streaming API calls beginning 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. The errors manifest as 502/503 responses from the API gateway for new requests while long-lived streaming sessions remain active. Impact: ~18% error rate for streaming endpoints for Ledgerly's tenant; only observed in us-east region. Customer-facing impact: degraded UX for live chat and transcript streaming, increased client retries.
impact_details:
- Affects Ledgerly (enterprise customer using dedicated tenant in us-east)
- Error types: 502 Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable, occasional 504 for long polling
- Estimate: 14-22% of streaming requests failed between 09:12–11:35 UTC on 2026-03-10 (rolling metrics)
- No billing discrepancy reported; primarily availability/latency degradation
environment_notes: Prod (dedicated tenant) on cluster us-east-a. Customer had multiple long-lived streaming sessions with high token output (average response sizes > 25k tokens per session) and clients using older HTTP/2 client library with small TCP write windows.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a long-lived streaming session to redwood-v2-large in us-east.
2) Simulate a slow client writer: send initial headers, then throttle data frames to 10 KB/s (small write window).
3) Open 40 concurrent short-lived streaming requests from a different client identity while the slow session is active.
4) Observe new requests returning 502/503 from API gateway after connection pool exhaustion and proxy timeouts.
observed_logs:
[2026-03-10T09:21:05Z] apigw[edge-01] WARN conn_pool: tenant=ledgerly sockets_in_use=120 max=128 waiting=42
[2026-03-10T09:21:08Z] apigw[edge-01] ERROR upstream: got 503 from upstream (upstream_timeout) request_id=abc123
[2026-03-10T09:22:10Z] runtime[worker-7] WARN threadpool: blocked_threads=47 total_threads=48 telemetry-flush stuck request=stream-xyz
[2026-03-10T09:23:02Z] runtime[worker-7] FATAL oom_protect: worker process crashed (SIGABRT) pid=33412
[2026-03-10T09:23:07Z] orchestrator INFO restart: worker pid=33412 restarted (same host)
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: simple connection-pool exhaustion at API gateway due to high number of long-lived streams.
- Confirmed that ledgerly had multiple streams that did not perform regular client-side flushing (slow writers) which held socket slots open for >2 minutes.
- Deeper trace: runtime threadpool metrics show a single worker with a telemetry flush (background telemetry aggregator) intermittently taking CPU and blocking scheduling of small tasks; combined with runtime's per-worker max concurrency, short-lived requests queued up, waiting on worker availability.
- The blocked thread combined with blocked sockets at the proxy produced head-of-line conditions: new requests could not get a free connection and the gateway returned 502/503 after its internal timeout.
- Recreated locally with slow-client simulator and observed identical error pattern and threadpool blocking in runtime logs.
- Related to INT-7682 (previous threadpool tuning experiment) — regression likely introduced by the telemetry-flush change that reduced fairness for incoming RPCs under heavy long-lived stream load.
customer_communications: 2026-03-10 09:27 UTC - Support (Eleanor): Notified Ledgerly of elevated error rates. Requested sample request IDs and approximate session durations.
2026-03-10 09:46 UTC - Customer (Ledgerly - S. Nguyen): Provided session IDs and client library version (http2 v0.9.1). Noted that streams were open for up to 14 minutes on large outputs.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Support (Diego): Shared initial mitigation: limiting concurrent short-lived sockets and asking customer to patch client to flush more frequently as immediate workaround.
2026-03-10 10:40 UTC - Support (Diego): Confirmed reduction in 5xx after gateway pool tuning and rolling restart of affected runtime worker.
2026-03-10 11:10 UTC - Customer (Ledgerly - S. Nguyen): Noted improvement to UX but asked for permanent fix and postmortem.
2026-03-12 15:03 UTC - Support (Eleanor): Sent preliminary incident summary and link to follow-up runbook update.
resolution:
Mitigation performed 2026-03-10 10:15 UTC: adjusted per-tenant connection pool soft limits (reduced long-lived socket reservation), increased API gateway internal socket timeout to avoid premature upstream failure, and applied emergency restart to the single runtime worker exhibiting telemetry-flush pinning. Deployed runtime patch (commit a9f3d2) to move telemetry flush to low-priority cooperative task to prevent thread starvation.
Workaround provided to customer: upgrade HTTP/2 client library to v0.9.3 and enable periodic small-frame flush (every 2s) to avoid holding sockets indefinitely.
Current status: error rates for Ledgerly returned to baseline (~<1%) by 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC. Monitoring alerts created for head-of-line socket hold and runtime blocked-thread ratio.
postmortem_action_items: Update streaming runbook: add detection for slow-client head-of-line and recommended mitigation steps (contrib: Diego)
Add integration test: simulate slow-client writes + concurrent short requests to verify fairness under real config (owner: runtime team)
Revert/tune telemetry-flush schedule if further regressions seen and instrument thread run-queue metrics (owner: infra-observability)
Consider per-tenant long-lived-stream reservation token to prevent aggressive pool exhaustion (owner: api-gateway)
Follow up with Ledgerly to confirm client patch rollout and collect post-fix telemetry (owner: CSM)
Create automated alert: runtime.blocked_thread_ratio > 0.2 AND apigw.waiting_connections > 20 for >2m (owner: SRE)
notes: This incident highlights an intersection failure mode: slow client writers can create resource starvation when combined with a single-threaded blocking pattern in the runtime. Fix includes both customer-facing guidance and a platform change to reduce scheduling priority of telemetry and other background work.
public_status_page_note: Investigigation complete. A small number of tenants experienced elevated 5xx for streaming endpoints due to long-lived client connections combined with background thread scheduling interactions; mitigations rolled out and fixed for impacted tenants. Full postmortem to follow.
